comparison: Both address claims C1-C4 regarding salicylate's IC50 and selectivity for CBP/p300. OpenEval finds the data directly supportive, while peer reviewers express concern that the IC50 of 10mM is too high to demonstrate specific and biologically relevant inhibition, requesting additional validation.

Both address thermal stability data (C5-C7). OpenEval also includes kinetic analysis (C8-C10) which peer result R2 partially covers. OpenEval finds all data supported, and peer reviewers do not raise specific concerns about binding or mechanism of inhibition data, noting experiments were 'rigorously examined'.

Both address kinetic analysis claims (C8-C10). OpenEval finds the Lineweaver-Burk analysis clearly supports competitive and noncompetitive inhibition patterns. Peer reviewers accept the binding and mechanism data without specific concerns.

Both address cellular acetylation data (C11-C14). OpenEval finds the Western blot data and IC50 values well-supported. Peer reviewers express concern that selective inhibition of some but not all p300/CBP-dependent modifications raises mechanistic questions about specificity.

Both address unchanged histone marks (C16, C18). OpenEval finds the data supported though explanations remain speculative. Peer reviewers are concerned that the selective pattern of inhibition is not adequately explained mechanistically.

Both address rescue experiments with p300 overexpression (C19-C24). OpenEval finds strong support from dose-dependent rescue and specificity data. Peer reviewers agree these are 'rigorously examined' and represent 'key rescue experiments' supporting the mechanism.

Both address non-histone substrate acetylation (C25-C27). OpenEval finds the NF-κB and p53 data strengthen conclusions. Peer reviewers specifically requested this demonstration of specificity and appear satisfied with the provided data.

Both address AMPK independence (C28-C33). OpenEval finds the control experiments effectively rule out AMPK as mediator. Peer reviewers accept these experiments as addressing off-target effect concerns without raising specific critiques.

Both address in vitro screening of related compounds (C36-C41). OpenEval finds the IC50 values and potency comparisons well-supported. Peer reviewers do not raise specific concerns about these in vitro screening findings.

Both address diflunisal cellular acetylation (C44-C49). OpenEval finds the IC50 and pharmacokinetic comparisons appropriate. Peer reviewers raise significant concern about the discrepancy between in vitro IC50 (1mM) and cellular IC50 (100μM), finding it strange and inadequately explained.

Both address diflunisal rescue experiments (C51-C52). OpenEval finds the data provide strong evidence for p300 as target. Peer reviewers note diflunisal 'hasn't been characterized to the same degree' as salicylate and request additional experiments, finding characterization incomplete.

OpenEval R11 addresses diflunisal effects on non-histone substrates (C53-C54) while peer R10 addresses AMPK independence (C55-C59). Both relate to diflunisal mechanism. OpenEval finds support, peer reviewers accept AMPK independence data without specific critiques.

Both address diflunisal AMPK independence (C55-C59). OpenEval finds the data parallel salicylate findings and strengthen AMPK-independent conclusions. Peer reviewers accept these control experiments without raising specific concerns.

Both address anti-leukemic effects in Kasumi-1 cells (C61-C67). OpenEval finds strong support from convergence of multiple assays. Peer reviewers express concern about specificity, requesting testing in other cell lines and more complete mechanistic validation of AML1-ETO acetylation as the cause.

Both address p300 overexpression rescue in leukemia cells (C74-C77). OpenEval finds strong evidence that p300 inhibition mediates anti-leukemic effects. Peer reviewers specifically requested these rescue experiments and appear satisfied with the provided data.

Both address xenograft tumor reduction (C78-C81). OpenEval finds dramatic effects clearly shown but notes lack of statistical analysis and sample sizes. Peer reviewers request assessment of acetylation inhibition in vivo and mechanistic validation (target engagement, IHC), expressing uncertainty about whether anti-tumor effects are due to p300 inhibition.

Both address CoA metabolite formation and potency (C100-C101, C103-C104). OpenEval finds substantial potency increase but questions whether metabolites form at sufficient cellular concentrations. Peer reviewers note this may explain conflicting data but caution that in vitro data may not be relevant, recommending demonstration of metabolite formation in cells.

Both address in vitro vs cellular IC50 discrepancy (C127-C129). OpenEval finds C127 supported but explanations largely speculative, noting CoA metabolites likely contribute. Peer reviewers note explanations were provided in rebuttal but not adequately incorporated into manuscript discussion, requesting this be added for readers.

OpenEval addresses H3K56 as most sensitive mark (C115-C117), finding support from dose-response comparisons and literature consistency. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval addresses cell cycle and differentiation effects (C68-C73), finding support from stated but not shown data with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though lack of presented data is noted as limitation.

OpenEval addresses negative results with other NSAIDs (C141-C143), noting data not shown prevents full evaluation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these negative control experiments.

OpenEval addresses main study conclusions (C82-C85, C144), finding strong support from convergence of multiple lines of evidence. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation of these summary conclusions found.
